stern.summary: German psychologist who introduced the concept of the intelligence quotient (IQ)

terman.summary: American psychologist who revised the Binet scale as the Stanford-Binet and launched a long-term study of gifted children

wechsler.summary: Romanian-born American psychologist who developed the Wechsler intelligence scales

flynn.summary: New Zealand political scientist who documented the generational rise in IQ scores

allport.summary: American psychologist who founded trait theory of personality and pioneered the study of prejudice

eysenck.summary: German-born British psychologist who proposed the PEN model of personality and promoted behavior therapy; later criticized over data issues

cronbach.summary: American educational psychologist who proposed the alpha coefficient and the concept of construct validity

meehl.summary: American psychologist who compared clinical judgment with statistical prediction and, with Cronbach, proposed construct validity

rasch.summary: Danish mathematician who proposed the Rasch model

mischel.summary: Austrian-born American psychologist who led the person-situation debate and conducted the marshmallow study of delayed gratification

gardner.summary: American developmental psychologist who proposed the theory of multiple intelligences

sternberg.summary: American psychologist who proposed the triarchic theory of intelligence

costa.summary: American psychologist who developed the NEO personality inventory with McCrae

mccrae.summary: American psychologist and a leading proponent of the Big Five model of personality

goldberg.summary: American psychologist who popularized the term "Big Five" and tested the lexical hypothesis

roberts.summary: American psychologist who studies how personality changes with age

simmons.summary: American behavioral scientist and first author of "False-Positive Psychology"

nelson.summary: American behavioral scientist and co-author of "False-Positive Psychology"

simonsohn.summary: Behavioral scientist who co-authored "False-Positive Psychology" and later exposed several cases of data fabrication

nosek.summary: American psychologist who led the Reproducibility Project in psychology and founded the Center for Open Science

ioannidis.summary: Greek-American epidemiologist who published "Why Most Published Research Findings Are False" in 2005

bem.summary: American psychologist who proposed self-perception theory; his 2011 precognition experiments unexpectedly became a trigger for the replication crisis

hall.summary: American psychologist who launched the child study movement and founded the American Psychological Association

piaget.summary: Swiss psychologist who founded the theory of cognitive development in children

vygotsky.summary: Soviet psychologist who founded sociocultural theory and died young at age 37

bruner.summary: American psychologist who took part in the cognitive revolution, introduced the idea of "scaffolding," and promoted cognitive approaches to education

erikson.summary: German-born American psychoanalyst who proposed eight stages of psychosocial development and the concept of "identity crisis"

marcia.summary: Canadian psychologist who developed an interview method for identity statuses

bowlby.summary: British psychoanalyst who founded attachment theory, linking psychoanalysis, ethology and developmental research

ainsworth.summary: Canadian-born American psychologist who designed the Strange Situation procedure and identified attachment styles

harlow.summary: American psychologist whose rhesus monkey experiments challenged the behaviorist account of maternal love

hazan.summary: American psychologist who proposed adult attachment with Shaver

shaver.summary: American psychologist and one of the founders of adult attachment research

kohlberg.summary: American psychologist who proposed the stages of moral development

gilligan.summary: American psychologist who proposed the ethics of care and criticized Kohlberg's male bias

bronfenbrenner.summary: American developmental psychologist who proposed ecological systems theory and helped establish the Head Start program

baumrind.summary: American developmental psychologist who proposed authoritative, authoritarian and permissive parenting styles

baltes.summary: German developmental psychologist and a leading founder of lifespan developmental psychology

premack.summary: American psychologist who asked in 1978 whether chimpanzees have a theory of mind

wimmer.summary: Austrian developmental psychologist who designed the false-belief task with Perner

perner.summary: Austrian developmental psychologist who studies the development of children's theory of mind

baron-cohen.summary: British psychologist who studies autism and theory of mind

baillargeon.summary: Canadian-born American psychologist who used infant experiments to study object permanence

spelke.summary: American psychologist who proposed the theory of "core knowledge"

saffran.summary: American psychologist who studies statistical learning in infants

gopnik.summary: American developmental psychologist who studies infant learning and causal reasoning

meltzoff.summary: American psychologist who studies imitation in infants

kuhl.summary: American language development researcher who studies speech sound learning in infants

le-bon.summary: French social psychologist and author of "The Crowd"

lewin.summary: German-born American psychologist, a pioneer of social psychology and organizational development, who came out of the Berlin Gestalt school

schein.summary: American organizational psychologist who proposed three levels of organizational culture and was strongly influenced by Lewin

vroom.summary: Canadian-born American organizational psychologist who proposed expectancy theory of work motivation

asch.summary: Polish-born American psychologist who designed the line-judgment experiments on conformity

milgram.summary: American psychologist who designed the obedience experiments and the "small world" study of six degrees of separation

cialdini.summary: American psychologist who studies persuasion and compliance, and author of "Influence"

zimbardo.summary: American psychologist who designed the Stanford prison experiment

darley.summary: American psychologist who researched the bystander effect

latane.summary: American social psychologist who, with Darley, proposed the bystander effect

adorno.summary: German philosopher and sociologist who led research on the authoritarian personality

steele.summary: American social psychologist who proposed stereotype threat

aronson.summary: American social psychologist who studied cognitive dissonance and invented the "jigsaw classroom" to reduce prejudice

greenwald.summary: American psychologist and a leading developer of the Implicit Association Test

festinger.summary: American social psychologist who proposed cognitive dissonance and social comparison theories, and was a student of Lewin

heider.summary: Austrian-born American psychologist, a founder of attribution theory, influenced by Gestalt psychology

ross.summary: American social psychologist who coined the term "fundamental attribution error"

doi.summary: Japanese psychiatrist who proposed the concept of "amae"

hwang.summary: Taiwanese psychologist who proposed a model of renqing and face, and advocated the indigenization of the social sciences

yang-kuo-shu.summary: Taiwanese psychologist who promoted the indigenous Chinese psychology movement from the 1980s

tajfel.summary: Polish-born British psychologist who founded social identity theory

turner.summary: British social psychologist who worked with Tajfel and proposed self-categorization theory

fiske.summary: American social psychologist who co-authored "Social Cognition" with Taylor and studies stereotypes

bargh.summary: American psychologist who studies automatic social processing and social priming

rosenthal.summary: American psychologist who studied expectancy effects

markus.summary: American psychologist and a leading founder of cultural psychology

kitayama.summary: Japanese-born American psychologist who studies how culture shapes the self and cognition

shweder.summary: American cultural anthropologist and psychologist who advocated cultural psychology

hofstede.summary: Dutch social psychologist who proposed the theory of cultural dimensions

nisbett.summary: American psychologist who compared Eastern and Western ways of thinking

henrich.summary: American anthropologist who raised the problem of WEIRD samples in psychology

haidt.summary: American social psychologist who studies moral intuitions and political division

maslow.summary: American psychologist and a founder of humanistic psychology, known for the hierarchy of needs and self-actualization

frankl.summary: Austrian psychiatrist, a concentration camp survivor, and founder of logotherapy

rogers.summary: American psychologist who founded client-centered therapy and was the first to extensively record and study the counseling process

perls.summary: German-born American psychiatrist who founded Gestalt therapy

goodman.summary: American writer and social critic who co-authored "Gestalt Therapy" with Perls

may.summary: American existential psychologist who brought European existentialism to the United States

yalom.summary: American psychiatrist and a leading figure in existential psychotherapy and group therapy

becker.summary: American cultural anthropologist, author of "The Denial of Death," whose ideas inspired terror management theory

csikszentmihalyi.summary: Hungarian-born American psychologist who proposed the concept of "flow"

deci.summary: American psychologist and co-founder of self-determination theory

ryan.summary: American psychologist and co-founder of self-determination theory

lepper.summary: American psychologist who studied how rewards can undermine intrinsic interest

greenberg-leslie.summary: Canadian psychologist and founder of emotion-focused therapy

johnson-sue.summary: Canadian psychologist and founder of emotionally focused couple therapy, which brought attachment theory into couples therapy

fredrickson.summary: American psychologist who proposed the broaden-and-build theory

duckworth.summary: American psychologist who proposed and popularized "grit"

dweck.summary: American psychologist who proposed the growth mindset

brickman.summary: American psychologist who proposed the hedonic treadmill concept

janet.summary: French psychologist and physician who proposed the concept of dissociation, overshadowed for many years by Freud

charcot.summary: French neurologist who studied hysteria using hypnosis; Freud studied under him

breuer.summary: Austrian physician who co-authored "Studies on Hysteria" with Freud and was a pioneer of the "talking cure"

freud.summary: Austrian neurologist and founder of psychoanalysis

anna-freud.summary: Daughter of Sigmund Freud and a leading figure in child psychoanalysis and ego psychology

hartmann.summary: Austrian-born American psychoanalyst who proposed the "conflict-free ego sphere"

vaillant.summary: American psychiatrist who directed the Harvard Study of Adult Development and studied defense mechanisms and adaptation
